Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

prisoner noun

held in prison

also prisoners, inmate, detainee

classical

Sen. Ep. 5.7
Plin. Ep. 10.19.1
Suet. Tib. 61 (Lewis & Short)

custōdia, custōdiae f.

noun, first declension

a prisoner under guard; in the plural, the prisoners

The guarding, and so the person guarded: post-Augustan (Lewis & Short). Before then, a man held in prison is in custōdiā or in vinculīs.

Other words

  • captīvus, captīvī m.; captīva, captīvae f. — a prisoner, detainee

    noun, second declension (captīva, first) · also used · modern · Levi–Bini p. 21, s.v. detenuto

    Classically a prisoner of war (see prisoner, of war); Levi and Bini extend it to anyone held in detention.

Examples

  • Quemadmodum eadem catēna et custōdiam et mīlitem cōpulat

    Just as the same chain links the prisoner and the soldierSen. Ep. 5.7

  • utrum per pūblicōs cīvitātium servōs, quod ūsque adhūc factum, an per mīlitēs asservāre custōdiās dēbeam

    whether I ought to guard the prisoners with the cities’ public slaves, as has been done until now, or with soldiersPlin. Ep. 10.19.1

See also prison, prisoner, arrest.

SourcesLewis & Short: custodia · Lewis & Short: captivus

Enrico Levi and Arturo Bini, Il latino come lingua viva (1937), p. 21, s.v. detenuto.
